Question Choices: When a finite limit exists, what does lim x->a f(x) describe?
Question Answers: the value f(x) approaches near a|the value approached by f(x)|nearby behavior of f
Hints: A limit concerns inputs close to a.|The actual value at a may differ.
Solution: A limit describes values at inputs arbitrarily close to the target, excluding the target itself. Changing or leaving undefined the value at that one point does not change a limit. A finite two-sided limit requires the same finite approached value on both sides. Finite table samples suggest an estimate; they do not prove a limit. It describes the value f(x) approaches as x gets close to a.
